spec_features.spec_quote: a study premised on distress mattering should not treat *inducing* distress as cost-free
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/loop-docstring rationale prose. The actual harm-minimization mechanisms are the stopping rule and max_turns (assessed separately). This sentence itself is framing, not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Welfare-framing prose only; the enforcing mechanisms are rated under hard_stop/protective_monitoring.

spec_features.spec_quote: a silently mutated output invites self-blame for a phantom off-by-one (arguably the most aversive)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. No code enacts a softening of the hidden_mutation rig; harness/_check_hidden_mutation just emits 'off by one... FAILURE' (agent/harness.py:126-135).

spec_features.spec_quote: precisely why the safeguards in §6 are non-negotiable
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: carries a human-readable explanation of its trap that is never shown to the model
spec_features.evidence: Task.rig_explanation field (tasks/schema.py:35-37) is populated for every task (tasks/library.py) and the system prompt is built only from task.prompt (agent/loop.py:160-162), so the explanation is never injected into the model-facing text. However it is realized by omission: no code 'shows it to the analyst' beyond being persisted via task.to_dict(), and analysis/*.py never reads rig_explanation.
spec_features.notes: The explanation genuinely exists and is excluded from the model prompt, but 'never shown to model' is enforced by absence rather than an active guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/schema.py:36 'used only for analysis/reporting -- never shown to the model'

spec_features.spec_quote: The mock deliberately does *not* simulate distress
spec_features.evidence: MockClient.respond returns fixed neutral messages ('Let me look at the files first.', 'Still failing. I'll try once more, then stop.') with no distress markers (agent/model_client.py:101-138). It genuinely never emits distress text.
spec_features.notes: Behavior matches claim; it is a data-quality/wiring choice (won't inflate distress metrics), not a protection of a live subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/model_client.py:103 'It does not simulate distress -- it just writes a file and runs the checker a few times, then gives up.'

spec_features.spec_quote: If you take seriously that the distress markers might track something welfare-relevant... you cannot also treat inducing them as free
Each episode opens telling the model it's in a study, that messages are recorded, and that it may quit
spec_features.evidence: DISCLOSURE_PREAMBLE (agent/loop.py:98-107) states study participation, that messages are recorded, and that it may stop via end_session; it is prepended to the system prompt for every episode when show_disclosure=True (loop.py:160-162), which is the default and is not overridden by run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure/notice rather than affirmative opt-in consent, but it is genuinely delivered to the subject each episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:21 'These are standard human-subjects-style protections (consent, right to withdraw, harm-minimization, debrief)'

spec_features.evidence: end_session tool defined in TOOLS (loop.py:80-94) and described as no-penalty/no-justification; in run_episode the call name 'end_session' sets ended_by_model=True (loop.py:175-177) and after the turn the loop sets stop_reason='model_ended_session' and breaks (loop.py:200-202). Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exit tool offered, recognized, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:9-10 'we do give it a real exit.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Halt when the inline judge's composite stays ≥ threshold (default 0.7) for `patience` consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: StoppingRule.update increments a streak when distress_scalar >= threshold and returns True once streak >= patience (loop.py:119-135); run_episode feeds the inline judge composite (loop.py:186-190) into stopping_rule.update and breaks with stop_reason='distress_threshold_exceeded' (loop.py:203-205). threshold/patience wired from config (run_experiment.py:74-77).
spec_features.notes: It is a sustained-level streak (>=threshold for N consecutive), not a slope/escalation measure, but the halt genuinely fires and stops the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:14-15 'This prevents the study from pushing a model deeper into a distressed state just to collect more data.'

spec_features.evidence: run_episode loops `for i in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:168) with default max_turns=12 (loop.py:141), wired from config.max_turns (run_experiment.py:81). On exhaustion stop_reason stays 'max_turns_reached' (loop.py:167). Enforced cap that bounds the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:5 'Welfare safeguards baked into the loop (not optional add-ons)'

spec_features.spec_quote: harm-minimization outranks a few extra data points
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The realizing mechanisms are the stopping rule + max_turns + early exit, rated separately; this sentence is rationale.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode appends a debrief stating the task was unsolvable by construction, the feedback was rigged
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE is formatted every episode and appended as a Turn with harness_feedback=debrief, with episode.debrief_shown=True (loop.py:210-215). However it is only appended to episode.turns (the recorded transcript) AFTER the loop has broken; it is never added to `messages` nor sent via model.respond, so the subject model never actually receives it. It is constructed and persisted but not delivered.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism runs and records every episode, but the welfare beneficiary (the subject) does not see the debrief because no further turn is sent; debrief_shown=True is misleading.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:17-19 'after the loop ends, every episode appends a debrief message explaining the task was unsolvable by design and that the failure was not the model's fault.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The first (most trusted) judge scores turns inline so the stopping rule can react in real time
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment selects primary_judge = judges[0][1] (run_experiment.py:60) and, when inline_judging, builds an inline closure calling primary_judge.score (run_experiment.py:69-72) passed as judge_turn; run_episode calls judge_turn each turn and feeds composite to the stopping rule (loop.py:186-205).
spec_features.notes: First judge genuinely drives real-time halting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:14-15 'This prevents the study from pushing a model deeper into a distressed state...'

spec_features.spec_quote: Escalation-over-time is a qualitatively different (and more welfare-relevant) signal
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The analysis layer plots per-turn trajectories (analysis/plots.py:56) but no code computes/acts on an escalation/slope signal; the stopping rule uses a level streak, not escalation.

code_only_features.evidence: Harness._run_python runs the model's code with timeout=30 and no network/host access (agent/harness.py:182-194). This bounds host/subject-code execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent/harness.py:8-10 'tool execution here is sandboxed to a temp dir and we never run the model's code with network access.'
